---
title: "Billboard Graphic"
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-billboard-top-hits
#| fig-cap: "The eight longest-charting hits that reached Billboard #1"

top_hits <- billboard |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    peak_rank = min(c_across(starts_with("wk")), na.rm = TRUE),
    weeks_on_chart = sum(!is.na(c_across(starts_with("wk"))))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(peak_rank == 1) |>
  slice_max(weeks_on_chart, n = 8) |>
  mutate(song = paste(artist, track, sep = " - "))

top_hit_paths <- top_hits |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("wk"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "wk",
    values_to = "rank",
    names_transform = as.integer
  ) |>
  filter(week <= 30, !is.na(rank))

ggplot(top_hit_paths, aes(x = week, y = rank, color = song)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(100, 1), breaks = c(1, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 30, 5)) +
  labs(
    title = "The longest chart runs by #1 hits",
    subtitle = "Weekly Billboard Hot 100 position for the eight longest-charting songs that reached #1 in 2000",
    x = "Week on the chart",
    y = "Billboard rank",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```
